Their centers are actual analytic sections on those charts.* 2. *On each chart, the clusters of $T_{j+1}$ refine those of $T_j$, and a fixed further refinement $j\mapsto j+N$ puts every child cluster in its parent with the radius ratio required in 25. The same $N$ works for every $j$, for all compact parameters, and on the finitely many support shells used for excision.* 3. *The cluster bounds have separated outer collars inside the enlarged output chart. Their intersection is $Z$, and their complements admissibly exhaust $X\setminus Z$.* *For $\mathscr F=\mathcal O^\flat$ or $\mathbb F_p$, put $$E_j=\operatorname{fib}\bigl(\mathbf R\Gamma(X,\mathscr F) \longrightarrow\mathbf R\Gamma(X\setminus T_j,\mathscr F) \bigr).$$ The inverse systems $H^0(E_j)$ and $H^1(E_j)$ are pro-zero. The same assertion holds relatively on the base and with compact parameters. Consequently the complex with support in $Z$ has no cohomology in degrees zero or one, and deletion of $Z$ preserves relative degree-zero sections. These conclusions hold also after a bounded-below descent calculation for which the finite chart refinements above can be made in each fixed total degree.* *For a closed locus $Z\subset Y$ in a possibly unbounded relative untilted affine space, the same low-degree support vanishing and degree-zero deletion statement hold if $Y$ has a compatible countable admissible exhaustion by interleaved bounds $X_a$ on which these hypotheses hold for $Z\cap X_a$. The tube systems and their required refinements may depend on $a$.

Let $L$ be a lattice of rank $e$ in a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q_p$-vector space, and let $L'=p^{-1}L$. With trivial characteristic-$p$ coefficients, continuous cohomology is the exterior algebra on $\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathrm{cts}}(L,\mathbb F_p)$. Under the identifications from a lattice basis,*

1.  *restriction from $L'$ to $L$ is zero in positive degrees and is the identity in degree zero;*

2.  *corestriction from $L$ to $L'$ is zero in degrees less than $e$ and identifies the top-degree orientation lines.*

*The assertions hold with coefficients $R_{\mathcal D}$ and with relative base complexes in place of $\mathbb F_p$.

For every $s\geq 0$ there are natural comparisons $$\begin{aligned}
 \mathbf R\Gamma_c(\mathcal N_m^s\times\underline{\mathcal D},\mathbb F_p)
   &\simeq E_{\mathcal D}[-(m+2)s],
       \label{eq:ind-whole-fp}\\
 \mathbf R\Gamma_c(\mathcal N_m^s\times\underline{\mathcal D},\mathcal O^\flat)
   &\simeq R_{\mathcal D}[-(m+2)s].
       \label{eq:ind-whole-flat}
\end{aligned}$$ A geometric Kummer orientation is understood. The comparison from the first formula to the second is extension of constants. It is compatible with continuous compact families of automorphisms and with all the support and lattice maps used below.

Let a quasicompact perfectoid chart over $C^\flat$ carry untilted coordinates $z_1,\ldots,z_t$ whose classes in $\mathcal N_m$ are independent. Restrict to a bounded part of this chart and to a compact open slope patch in $\mathbb Q_p^t$. After a finite refinement of the base by quasicompact charts, the following constructions are available on each member of the refinement.*


1.  *There are radii $0<\alpha<\beta$ and a fixed lattice $L\subset \mathbb Q_p^t\oplus F_m$ such that, on every geometric fiber, $$\label{eq:ind-persistent-lattice}
           L=\{w:|\ell_z(w)|\leq\alpha\}
            =\{w:|\ell_z(w)|<\beta\},
           \qquad
           \ell_z(a,b)=\sum_i a_i z_i+b.$$ The same base chart has lattice $p^jL$ for the radii $\alpha|p|^j$ and $\beta|p|^j$, for every integer $j$.*

2.  *Write $L_a=\operatorname{pr}_{\mathbb Q_p^t}(L)$ and $L_b=L\cap F_m$. At every sufficiently large $j$, the slope patch is a finite union of $p^jL_a$-cosets. Its graph in $\mathcal N_m$ has disjoint tubular neighborhoods indexed by those cosets. Each tube is the image of an actual relative disc, centered at a section $\sum_i a_i z_i$ for a constant representative $a$, modulo the compact translation lattice $p^jL_b$.*

3.  *The closed tubes of radius $\alpha|p|^j$ and the open tubes of radius $\beta|p|^j$ are interleaved and cofinal among neighborhoods of the graph family. The construction works on a slightly enlarged independent-base bound and on its support collars, and it retains an arbitrary compact profinite parameter $\mathcal D$.*

*For finitely many added coordinates and compact open patches of matrices of slopes, take products of these constructions. Their finite base refinements can be chosen simultaneously.

There is a natural triangle $$\label{eq:ind-rank-triangle}
 \mathbf R\Gamma_c(X_{s,\geq t+1},\mathscr E)
 \longrightarrow \mathbf R\Gamma_c(X_{s,\geq t},\mathscr E)
 \longrightarrow \mathcal G_{s,t}(\mathscr E)
 \longrightarrow
 \mathbf R\Gamma_c(X_{s,\geq t+1},\mathscr E)[1],$$ where $\mathcal G_{s,t}$ is computed by shrinking neighborhood germs of $Z_{s,t}$, with compact support along that locus. Locally on a compact open Grassmannian graph patch $P$, it is $$\label{eq:ind-germ-formula}
  \operatorname{LC}\bigl(P,
           \mathbf R\Gamma_c(Y_t,\mathscr E)\bigr).$$ Here $\operatorname{LC}(P,-)$ means the filtered colimit of finite direct sums over finite clopen partitions of $P$. With an external compact parameter $\mathcal D$, the corresponding formula is $$\operatorname{LC}\bigl(P,
   \mathbf R\Gamma_c(Y_t\times\underline{\mathcal D},\mathscr E)\bigr).$$ At each tube depth only a finite partition of $P$ is used, while $\mathcal D$ remains in the base complex. The slope-partition colimit is algebraic.

Let $H$ be a compact $p$-adic analytic group and let $V$ be a countable smooth admissible $\mathbb F_p[H]$-module. Then $H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V)$ is finite-dimensional for every $a$. Let $H$ act trivially on the external parameter $\mathcal D$ and on $R_{\mathcal D}$, and diagonally through $V$ on $R_{\mathcal D}\otimes V$. For the coefficient topology supplied by uniform finite-span families, there is a natural isomorphism $$H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,R_{\mathcal D}\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}V)
 \cong R_{\mathcal D}\otimes_{\mathbb F_p}H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V).$$

Let $1\leq m19. Let $Z_U$ be the perfected analytic cover associated with $B_U$ over $$0<|x|<1,\qquad |y_i|<1.$$ Then $$H^j\mathbf R\Gamma\bigl(G,\mathbf R\Gamma_c(Z_U,\mathcal O^\flat)\bigr)$$ is finite-dimensional over $C^\flat$ for every integer $j$. With an external compact profinite parameter $\mathcal D$, the corresponding groups are obtained by extension to $R_{\mathcal D}$ and are finite over that ring.

For every $s\geq0$, $$\label{eq:ind-ordinary-functions}
 \Gamma(Y_s,\mathcal O^\flat)=C^\flat,
 \qquad
 \Gamma(Y_s\times\underline{\mathcal D},\mathcal O^\flat)
       =R_{\mathcal D}.$$ The identifications are by pullback of scalars. For $s\geq1$, projection $Y_s\to Y_{s-1}$ has relative degree-zero direct image $\mathcal O^\flat$.*

*Consequently a $G$-invariant algebraic function in a fixed finite marked coefficient model becomes a scalar after pullback to the completed full marking tower. If the model and its chosen component are defined over the finite field $k$, that scalar belongs to $k$. In particular this applies to invariant algebraic units.

Assume $m>1$. With the powers in [eq:trans-powers], there is a natural $G$-equivariant isomorphism $$V_{\mathop{\mathrm{Coind}}_q(E)}\simeq (V_E)^{1/h}. \label{eq:trans-root-functor}$$ It is compatible with the natural auxiliary actions and with every arrow of a finite diagram. It preserves exact diagrams and is compatible with successive coinduction and successive roots. For any fixed initial diagram, these assertions hold at every sufficiently deep finite marking stage, retaining the natural auxiliary action on each of its coinductions.

After one finite marking shrink to a pro-$p$ subgroup, $\widehat\Omega^1_{R/k}$ has a $G$-invariant frame. In particular it has a $G$-invariant volume generator $\eta\in\widehat\Omega^r_{R/k}$.*


*For a finite root order $h$ fixing $k$, the normalized Cartier functional $$T_{\eta,h}:R^{1/h}\longrightarrow R,
 \qquad T_{\eta,h}(z)=\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{C}}^{\log_p h}(z^h\eta)}{\eta}
 \label{eq:trans-cartier-functional}$$ is $R$-linear and generates $\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}_R(R^{1/h},R)$ as a module over $R^{1/h}$. A nonzero translation augmentation at the corresponding finite torsor level induces a scalar multiple of this functional; the scalar belongs to the chosen finite constant field.

At the finite marking stage of , the operator $$S(f)=\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{C}}^{\nu_0}(f\eta)}{\eta}\quad(f\in R)
 \label{eq:trans-S}$$ is continuous, $k$-linear, and $G$-equivariant. It satisfies $S(b^{h_0}f)=bS(f)$. For $m>1$, the maps on $R$ induced by nonzero translation augmentations $\mathsf N_{q_0^a}\to k$, after the root identification, are nonzero scalar multiples of $S^a$. For $m=1$ one can choose the toral frame so that $$S\mathop{\mathrm{Fr}}^{\nu_0}=1.
 \label{eq:trans-height-one-split}$$*


*Extend $S$ to $B'$ by $S(f)=S(ef)$, with image in $eB'$. There is a fixed integer $c\geq0$ such that, for every integer $D$, $$S(x^{-D}A')\subset x^{-\lceil D/h_0\rceil-c}A'.
 \label{eq:trans-pole-bound}$$ Every sufficiently large $D_0$ makes $\mathcal P=x^{-D_0}A'$ stable under $S$. Every fixed bounded-pole lattice, including any compact family of cochains with values in it, is carried into $\mathcal P$ by all sufficiently large iterates.*

*The volume, its inverse, the whole trace-pairing matrices and their inverses have one fixed pole bound $c'$. In the normalized basis $b_i^{1/h}$, $h=h_0^a$, their transported matrices have pole losses at most $c'/h$. The normalized Cartier maps are adjoint to the inclusions of root Laurent representatives under the residue pairings with the transported volumes.

Fix a finite Yoneda diagram of translation representations, descend it at a finite marking stage, and fix a cohomological degree. Its successive boundary maps can be represented by an operator on cocycles that loses at most one fixed $x$-pole order. Under , all of its coinduced diagrams use the roots of this same operator and its chosen splittings.

The $G$-action on $W$ and on $\mathscr W_{\mathcal D}$ is jointly continuous from a complete step, with a compact set of group and parameter values, into a complete step. It is uniformly equicontinuous there. The same holds for multiplication by the finite marked function algebra, fixed root-basis changes, and the finite matrices occurring in continuous group resolutions. Absolute Frobenius is an invertible additive operator on these modules. Its sufficiently divisible powers fixing $k$ commute with $G$ and act by chain automorphisms on the group complexes over $k$.

At every sufficiently deep product marking level used in 35, both $H^a_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,W)$ and $H_i^{\mathrm{cts}}(G,W)$ are finite-dimensional over $k$ for every $a,i\geq0$. Since $k$ is finite, these are finite groups.

The finite-level pairings extend uniquely to an exact sequence of $k[G]$-modules $$0\longrightarrow W_+\longrightarrow W
   \xrightarrow{\ \pi\ }Q\longrightarrow0.
 \label{eq:cutoff-residue-sequence}$$ The map $\pi$ is continuous on every complete coefficient step into the discrete countable module $Q$, including on compact parameter families. It is equivariant for the actual group actions on the support and compact-dual models. All these assertions allow arbitrary root denominators in $W$.

For every integer $\nu\geq0$ and every tuple $w\in W_+^\nu$, there are an integer $a_*\geq0$, a complete weighted step written in the original whole basis, and $\epsilon,\alpha>0$ such that all $\Phi^{a_*+a}w$ belong to the closed subspace with x-order at least $\epsilon$, and $$\|\Phi^{a_*+a}w\|\leq
       \exp(-\alpha h_0^a)\quad(a\geq0).
 \label{eq:cutoff-contraction}$$ The statement applies without a bound on the root denominators of the coefficient series.

Let $Z$ be a Polish topological group and $B\subseteq Z$ an analytic subgroup in the sense of descriptive set theory: $B$ is a continuous image of a Polish space. If $Z/B$ is countable, then $B$ is open.
For the completed-resolution group homology of 2, $$H_i(G,W_+)=0\qquad(i\geq0).$$

For every $i\geq0$ the compact vector space $M_i=H^i(G,\mathcal P)$ satisfies $$I_i:=\bigcap_{a\geq0}S^aM_i\quad\text{is finite}.
 \label{eq:cutoff-stable}$$ No uniform bound on its size as the prime, height, degree, or finite marking level varies is asserted.

Let $M$ be a profinite $k$-vector space and let $S:M\to M$ be a continuous linear map. Assume that $I=\bigcap_{a\geq0}S^aM$ and $M/SM$ are finite. Then $S$ is an automorphism of $I$, and $V=M/I$ is a finitely generated $k[[z]]$-module with $z$ acting by $S$. Its original topology is the z-adic topology. The locally nilpotent subgroup $$T_S(M)=\bigcup_{a\geq0}\ker(S^a:M\to M)$$ is finite and closed. In particular $\ker S$ is finite.

Fix $i\geq0$ and $N\geq1$. Suppose $$S^NX_i/S^{N+1}X_i\quad\text{is countable}.
 \label{eq:cutoff-consecutive-hypothesis}$$ Then $S^NM_i/S^{N+1}M_i$ is finite, and $(S^NM_i)/I_i$ is a finitely generated $k[[z]]$-module with $z=S$. The operator $S$ on $S^NX_i$ has countable kernel and cokernel. Moreover $\ker(f_i|_{S^NM_i})$ is finite and closed, $f_i$ is injective on $I_i$, and $$\bigcap_{a\geq0}\mathop{\mathrm{im}}(S^aM_i\longrightarrow X_i)
      =f_i(I_i)\cong I_i.
 \label{eq:cutoff-localized-intersection}$$ In particular the intersection is finite. No topology on $X_i$ and no closed-image assertion for its cochain differential is required.

Assume the next-height coefficient-finiteness hypothesis of 17. There is an index $ u_0$ such that $$H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,B_{U_ u}) \quad ext{is countable-dimensional over $k$}$$ for every $ u\geq u_0$ and every integer $i$.

For an abelian category $\mathcal B$, the constant objects in $\operatorname{Pro}(\mathcal B)$ are closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between them, and under extensions. If a decreasing system of subobjects $J_a\subset X$ represents a constant subobject $I\subset X$ in $\operatorname{Pro}(\mathcal B)$, then $J_a=I$ for all sufficiently large $a$.

For every $i$, the pro-object $\overline T^{\,i}(\Lambda)$ is constant, and its canonical projection to $T^i(k)$ is monic. It is annihilated by $\mathfrak m$. Moreover, there is an integer $N_i\geq1$, independent of the sufficiently deep marking level, such that $$S^{N_i}X^i_
u/S^{N_i+1}X^i_
u
 \quad	ext{is countable-dimensional for all sufficiently large $
u$}.$$

For finite-length $\Lambda$-modules $E,F$, the natural map $$\operatorname{Ext}^j_{\mathcal C}(E,F)
       \longrightarrow \operatorname{Ext}^j_\Lambda(E,F)$$ is an isomorphism for every $j$. Here the left side is Yoneda Ext: its classes are represented by exact diagrams whose middle terms all have finite length.

Suppose $T^\bullet(k)$ is not zero, and let $b$ be its largest nonzero degree. There is an allowed power index $s=q_0^{a_s}$ and a generator $$e_s\in\operatorname{Ext}^d_\Lambda(\mathsf N_s,k)$$ whose operation is an epimorphism in $\mathcal A$: $$e_s:T^{b-d}(\mathsf N_s)\longrightarrow T^b(k).$$

Let $U$ be a uniform pro-$p$ marking subgroup, and let $E,F$ be finite objects of $\mathcal R_U$. Each group $\operatorname{Ext}^j_{\mathcal R_U}(E,F)$ is finite. There is one open subgroup $U'\subset U$ on which every element of the kernel of $$\operatorname{Ext}^j_{\mathcal R_U}(E,F)
      \longrightarrow\operatorname{Ext}^j_T(E,F)$$ becomes zero.

For every $1\leq m\leq n$, every coefficient module $M$ in over $A_m$, and every $i\geq0$, the group $$H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}(P_n,M)$$ is finite. In particular, this holds for every integer periodicity twist of $A_m$.

Assume the coefficient finiteness assertion at height $m+1$. For a basic coefficient $M$ over $A_m$, including any fixed tensor product of the basic division-tuple coefficients and an integer periodicity twist, there is a sufficiently deep normal product level $U$ such that $$H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}\bigl(G,B_U\otimes_{A_m}M\bigr)$$ is countable for every $i\geq0$. The same conclusion holds after further shrinking within the chosen cofinal sequence.

Let $M_B$ be a finite locally free $B$-module with the coefficient action of $G$, and let $U\triangleleft J$ be a finite marking level. If $$H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,B_U\otimes_B M_B)$$ is countable for every $i\geq0$, then $H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,M_B)$ is countable for every $i\geq0$. The order of $J/U$ need not be invertible in $k$.

Let $E_n$ be Morava $E$-theory for the height-$n$ Honda group over $\mathbb F_{p^n}$, and let $$\mathbb G_n=P_n\rtimes\mathop{\mathrm{Gal}}(\mathbb F_{p^n}/\mathbb F_p)$$ be its extended stabilizer. For every $i\geq0$ and every $t\in\mathbb Z$, both groups $$H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}\bigl(P_n,\pi_t(E_n/p)\bigr),\qquad
 H^i_{\mathrm{cts}}\bigl(\mathbb G_n,\pi_t(E_n/p)\bigr)$$ are finite.
For every prime $p$, every $n\geq1$, and every $j\in\mathbb Z$, the group $$\pi_jL_{K(n)}(S/p)$$ is finite.

Let $X$ be a derived $p$-complete spectrum. If $\pi_j(X/p)$ is finite for every $j\in\mathbb Z$, then $\pi_jX$ is finitely generated over $\mathbb Z_p$ for every $j\in\mathbb Z$. Conversely, finite generation of all $\pi_jX$ over $\mathbb Z_p$ implies finiteness of all $\pi_j(X/p)$.

Let $p$ be odd. Then, for every $j\in\mathbb Z$, $$\pi_jL_{K(1)}S_p^\wedge\cong
 \begin{cases}
  \mathbb Z_p, & j=0\text{ or }j=-1,\\
  \mathbb Z/p^{\,1+\nu_p(t)},
       & j=2t-1,\quad0\neq t\in(p-1)\mathbb Z,\\
  0, & \text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}$$ The displayed groups include all additive extensions.

coverage.checked_domain: The listed deterministic vectors with heights between 1 and 16, including the empty subset, a singleton, a repeated subset sum, the sum of all generator degrees, and degrees outside the attainable range.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact exhaustive enumeration of every subset for each listed input independently checks the dynamic-programming output. This is finite instance verification, not certification for every height or integer degree.
